security_spec.violation_condition: If the TlbCmd multiplexer at NewStoreUnit.scala:225 incorrectly assigns TlbCmd (e.g., cbo.clean/cbo.flush/cbo.inval receive TlbCmd.write instead of TlbCmd.read due to inverted isCboNoZero gate, or cbo.zero receives TlbCmd.read), the TLB permission check at TLB.scala:421-427 will verify the wrong access type (w instead of r or vice versa), and the PMP checker at PMP.scala:405-406 will apply the wrong permission bit (cfg.w instead of cfg.r). The hardware would grant access through PMP/TLB with insufficient or incorrect privilege verification.
security_spec.summary: XiangShan currently implements CBO permission checks correctly via implicit TlbCmd routing (read for cbo.clean/flush/inval, write for cbo.zero) in NewStoreUnit dispatch, with TLB/PMP both deriving access type from TlbCmd; violation would occur if TlbCmd assignment is corrupted, silently granting unprivileged access to cache-block operations across PMP/page-table boundaries

findings.finding: TlbCmd multiplexer correctly assigns TlbCmd.read to cbo.clean/flush/inval (isCboNoZero=true) and TlbCmd.write to cbo.zero (isCboNoZero=false). LSUOpType.isCbo (line 580) matches op(3,2)==='b11' && op(6,4)==='b000', which covers cbo_clean=0b1100, cbo_flush=0b1101, cbo_inval=0b1110 but NOT cbo_zero=0b0111 (bits 3:2=01). The Mux gate is NOT inverted — write path is the else/default, which is correct because cbo.zero writes zeros to the cache line and requires write permission per RISC-V spec.

TLB permission check correctly classifies TlbCmd-based CBO access. cbo.clean/flush/inval (TlbCmd.read) → isLd=true → checked against perm.r (load path, line 428). cbo.zero (TlbCmd.write) → isSt=true → checked against perm.w (store path, line 429). No bypass: the cmd value from the store unit's Mux flows directly into isLd/isSt classification.
findings.snippet:
val isLd = TlbCmd.isRead(cmd) && !TlbCmd.isAmo(cmd)
val isSt = TlbCmd.isWrite(cmd) || TlbCmd.isAmo(cmd)
...
val ldPermFail = !(modeCheck && Mux(hlvx, perm.x, perm.r || mxr(idx) && perm.x))
val stPermFail = !(modeCheck && perm.w)

findings.finding: PMP checker correctly derives permission bits from TlbCmd. cbo.clean/flush/inval (TlbCmd.read) → resp.ld = (!cfg.r) — treated as load, checked against cfg.r. cbo.zero (TlbCmd.write) → resp.st = (!cfg.w) — treated as store, checked against cfg.w. No cbo-specific bypass or short-circuit.

PMP inaccessible flag correctly handles both CBO categories. Operator precedence (&& > ||) gives: pmp.st || (pmp.ld && isCboNoZero). cbo.zero (isCboNoZero=false) → only pmp.st applies (correct: write permission). cbo.clean/flush/inval (isCboNoZero=true) → pmp.ld applies (correct: read permission). Note: lack of explicit parentheses around pmp.ld && isCboNoZero is a minor readability concern but produces correct hardware.

The memidx.is_st field is hardwired to true.B for all store-unit TLB requests (including CBO reads). However, TLB.scala's perm_check function does NOT reference memidx bits for permission decisions — it uses only the cmd field (TlbCmd.isRead/isWrite). Verified via grep: no memidx.is_st or memidx.is_ld references in TLB.scala. This field is metadata-only and does not affect the hardware permission path.

CBO fuOpType bit-field definitions are internally consistent. cbo_zero=0b0111 has bits 3:2=01 (distinct from clean/flush/inval which all have bits 3:2=11). isCbo() requires op(3,2)==='b11' AND op(6,4)==='b000', correctly distinguishing CBO from other operations sharing the b11 prefix in bits 3:2 (e.g., prefetch subtypes via bits 6:4). isCboAll() is the OR of isCbo and cbo_zero. No off-by-one errors in bit positions.
findings.snippet:
def cbo_zero  = "b0111".U
def cbo_clean = "b1100".U
def cbo_flush = "b1101".U
def cbo_inval = "b1110".U
def isCbo(op: UInt): Bool = op(3, 2) === "b11".U && (op(6, 4) === "b000".U)
def isCboAll(op: UInt): Bool = isCbo(op) || op(3,0) === cbo_zero

findings.finding: Decoder maps CBO instructions to correct LSUOpType values: CBO_CLEAN→cbo_clean, CBO_FLUSH→cbo_flush, CBO_INVAL→cbo_inval, CBO_ZERO→cbo_zero. All dispatched to FuType.stu. The decode-to-fuOpType mapping is consistent with the LSUOpType definitions — no encoding mismatch between decode and the TlbCmd Mux classification.
findings.snippet:
CBO_ZERO  -> XSDecode(SrcType.reg, SrcType.DC, SrcType.X, FuType.stu, LSUOpType.cbo_zero , ...)
CBO_CLEAN -> XSDecode(SrcType.reg, SrcType.DC, SrcType.X, FuType.stu, LSUOpType.cbo_clean, ...)
CBO_FLUSH -> XSDecode(SrcType.reg, SrcType.DC, SrcType.X, FuType.stu, LSUOpType.cbo_flush, ...)
CBO_INVAL -> XSDecode(SrcType.reg, SrcType.DC, SrcType.X, FuType.stu, LSUOpType.cbo_inval, ...)
